body:
## Summary
The human interview scorecard is one key inside the prep payload (`payload.humanScorecard`), replaced wholesale on every save and used to pre-fill the next person's form. A second interviewer, or a second interview round in a workspace that split the Interview column, silently erases the first record and starts anchored on it. Store human scorecards as a list keyed by (author, stage), seed each interviewer's form only from their own record, and keep `humanScorecard` as a derived headline mirror so every existing reader and a rollback stay intact.

## Description
The registry's structured-interview-scorecards golden path (section 'Independent scoring before the debrief') and interview-round-design ('assessments are recorded before they are compared') set the standard: each assessor commits an independent written score, and a second read never has access to the first. kp breaks this in three places at once. First, `saveHumanScorecard` (interview-prep.ts:153) replaces the single key. Second, the scorecard route gates by stage ROLE precisely so a workspace can split Interview into rounds (route.ts:158-160), yet every round's save lands in that one key. Third, `HumanScorecardPanel` seeds its form from `prep.humanScorecard` (Panel:52-66, Modal:140), so interviewer B opens A's ratings, evidence and verdict pre-filled and overwrites them on Save. The decision seal also records actor 'human:recruiter' (route.ts:142) with no author.

The move is a pure module, `app/_lib/human-scorecard-set.ts`: `HumanScorecardRecord = Scorecard & { author: string|null; authorLabel: string|null; stage: string|null; savedAt: string }`, `readHumanScorecards(payload)` (legacy single key becomes one author-null record), `upsertHumanScorecard(list, rec)` (replace on the same (author, stage), else append, capped at 12), `ownScorecard(list, author, stage)` and `headlineScorecard(list)` (the latest savedAt). `saveHumanScorecard(entryId, scorecard, key)` runs the upsert inside the existing `.immediate()` transaction (interview-prep.ts:150), which is already the lock-first read-then-write strategy, with no await inside, and writes both `humanScorecards` and the `humanScorecard` headline mirror in the same UPDATE. `getHumanScorecard` keeps its signature and returns the headline. `getHumanScorecards(entryId, workspaceId)` is the new scoped reader.

The scorecard route resolves `author = currentUser().userId` (null in open mode, which gives today's single slot per stage), `stage = pipelineEntry.stage`, and `authorLabel` from `getUserById` (imported from `app/_lib/db/users`, not the barrel). It adds the author to the seal's `inputs` and gains a GET that returns `{ mine, records }`, scoped by the same `getInterviewPrep(entry, ws)` read as the POST (gated route, already listed in api-reference.md:371, so no public-routes change; the api-reference row is regenerated with `npm run api:docs` for the new method).

Every surface that shows or offers a human scorecard is named here:
- Prep modal panel (the scoring surface): fetches `mine` and seeds only from it. The Modal stops passing `prep.humanScorecard`.
- Transcript modal (review surface): lists `records`, each labelled by author, through HumanScorecardSection.
- Drawer (candidate-timeline.ts:431 (was :425 at 7bd86775; r08 pipeline-candidate-drawer is editing this file, so re-grep `humanScorecard?: Scorecard } | undefined)?.humanScorecard` at build)), compare grid (compare/route.ts:79,95), Schedule card flag (interview-prep.ts:296-298) and Decisions queue (the approval payload, route.ts:172): these read the headline mirror and are deliberately unchanged in this card. Listing every panel member on the drawer and the compare grid is the named follow-up.

## Flow
1. Interviewer A (u1) opens the prep modal and clicks Score interview. GET scorecard returns `{mine:null}`, so the form is empty. A saves, and the store holds `[u1/interview]` with headline u1.
2. Interviewer B (u2) opens the same candidate. `mine` is null again, so the form is empty and not A's. B saves, and the store holds `[u1/interview, u2/interview]` with headline u2. A's record is untouched.
3. The candidate moves to 'Interview 2' (a split axis). A saves round 2, and the store holds three records. Round 1 survives.
4. The transcript modal shows all three, labelled. The drawer and compare grid show the headline, as they do today.

## Expected impact
No human interview record is ever destroyed by a colleague's or a later round's save. That is the data-loss class behind every panel or multi-round use. The pre-fill anchoring path closes, and the seal names its actor. Existing readers keep working through the mirror. Perf: server-only module plus a fetch in the panel. Nothing is added to the app/page.tsx or task-hub import graphs.

## Evaluation
Claim: human scorecards are per-(author, stage) records. A save replaces only its own record, and the scoring form never pre-fills another author's verdict.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass.
After: 8 of 8.
Method: gate — node:test on human-scorecard-set.test.ts (pure) and panel-scorecards.test.ts (the real POST/GET against unit-db, two principals, as stage-role.test.ts drives POST today), plus the integration gate (tsc, lint, i18n:check, api:check, test:unit).
Result: pending build.
Gate: contract (the stored payload gains a key and the scorecard route gains a GET. The legacy key is kept as a mirror).

title: Regenerate previews its changes: keep or replace, never a blind overwrite

body:
## Summary
Regenerate replaces the interview plan the moment the task finishes. The interviewer learns what changed, if ever, by noticing that a block they had woven questions into is gone or that their ticks moved. From the modal, stage the regenerated plan as `pendingPlan` instead. Show a computed diff of blocks added, removed and retimed, woven questions that would fall back to unassigned, and ticks that would detach. Replace or Keep is one click.

## Description
The registry technique regenerate-without-destroying-human-notes gets the merge half right, and kp implements that half (interview-prep-run.ts:98-103). Its step 6 is not implemented: 'Report what changed. A merge that reports nothing is functionally indistinguishable from one that destroyed everything.' Today three buttons offer the same blind action: the footer, the fallback banner and the stale-JD banner (Modal:66-73, Header:58-64, 74-81). The run overwrites in one pass (interview-prep-run.ts:79-85), and the modal swaps the plan in on completion (hook:147-167). Two consequences are fully computable in advance and shown to nobody. splitImported demotes a woven question whose block topic disappeared (progress.ts:51-62). Ticks keyed `c-<i>` (RunOfShow:39) re-attach by index.

The build:
1. `runInterviewPrep` honours `params.stage === true` when a pack already exists. It writes the generator-owned keys under `payload.pendingPlan` through a new `stageInterviewPrepPlan` in interview-prep.ts. That is a read-merge-write in `.immediate()` with no await inside, and it leaves created_at alone. With no prior pack it commits as today. An unstaged run deletes any `pendingPlan` before merging.
2. `acceptPendingPlan(entryId)` and `discardPendingPlan(entryId)` in interview-prep.ts, each an `.immediate()` transaction that re-reads the row and returns false when no pendingPlan exists. Accept overlays the pending generator keys onto the payload and moves created_at in the same UPDATE, so the stale chip and 'generated NN ago' follow truthfully.
3. PATCH `/api/interview-prep` accepts `{plan:'accept'|'discard'}` behind the same `pipeline:write` capability, throttle and tenancy read as the weave (route.ts:197-252). A missing pending plan answers 409 `INTERVIEW_PREP_NO_PENDING_PLAN`, a new REFUSAL_ERRORS code with four catalog entries. No new route, so neither public-routes.ts nor the api-reference method set changes.
4. `schedulePrepPlanDiff.ts` (pure, tested): `computePlanDiff(current, candidate, checked, importedEntries)` returns `{added, removed, retimed, wovenOrphaned, checkedDetached, durationFrom, durationTo, sourceFrom, sourceTo, isNoop}`. It reuses splitImported and prepProgress's key scheme, so the preview and the post-swap render cannot disagree.
5. The hook passes `stage:true` when a prep exists. A completion carrying `pendingPlan` sets pending state instead of `generated`. A GET that returns `payload.pendingPlan` restores the preview after a reopen (the recruiter closed the modal mid-generation).
6. `ScheduleInterviewPrepPlanDiff.tsx` renders the diff banner above the run-of-show with Replace plan and Keep current. An isNoop candidate says 'no changes' and offers Discard.

Every surface that offers regenerate or shows the plan is named here. The modal's three buttons are staged. The Decisions-queue accept (useDecisionsQueue.ts:441) and the voice-interview first-generation (interview-run.ts:475-482) stay direct, by design, because neither has a human watching a plan. The voice agenda, copy-out and Schedule card read the committed keys only, so a pending plan is invisible to them until accepted. Perf: one new client component in the Schedule tab chunk, nothing on app/page.tsx or the task-hub graph.

## Flow
1. The recruiter sees 'JD edited since 12 Sep' and clicks Regenerate. The task runs. The current plan stays on screen and usable.
2. On completion the banner reads: 2 blocks added, 1 removed ('System design'), 1 woven question returns to unassigned, 2 ticks will detach, 25 to 30 min.
3. Replace plan: PATCH accept, and the modal re-seeds from the accepted payload. Or Keep current: PATCH discard, and nothing changed.
4. Closing the modal before deciding is safe. The next open shows the same preview from the stored pendingPlan.

## Expected impact
Regeneration becomes a reviewed decision instead of an irreversible overwrite. The interviewer keeps a tailored plan when the new one is worse (a keyless fallback template replacing an AI plan is the sharpest case, since `sourceFrom`/`sourceTo` makes it explicit). The technique's missing step 6 becomes a rendered, tested fact.

## Evaluation
Claim: a modal-initiated regeneration never replaces the committed plan until the interviewer accepts a diff computed from the same rules the post-swap render uses.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass.
After: 8 of 8.
Method: gate — node:test on schedulePrepPlanDiff.test.ts (pure), interview-prep-run.test.ts (stage/unstaged with the automation stubbed as the existing test does), and pending-plan.test.ts (the real PATCH against unit-db), plus i18n:check for the new code and the integration gate.
Result: pending build.
Gate: none.
